problem:
Fill in the missing parts in the parametric equations below that describe all the points on the line segment $\overset{―}{PQ},$ where $P(4,-1,7)$ and $Q(-6,5,0).$

| $x=$ | {{field-1}} | $t\in [0,$ {{field-2}} $]$ |
| --- | --- | --- |
| $y=$ | {{field-3}} |  |
| $z=$ | $7-7t$ |  |
worked_solution:
First, we need to find a direction vector that is parallel to the line passing through the given points. We can use the vector $\overset{\to }{PQ}$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}v & =\overset{\to }{PQ} \\  & =\overset{\to }{OQ}-\overset{\to }{OP} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-6 \\ 5 \\ 0\end{aligned}]-[\begin{aligned}4 \\ -1 \\ 7\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-10 \\ 6 \\ -7\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

So, the vector equation of the line is

$$
\begin{aligned}r & =p+tv \\ r & =[\begin{aligned}4 \\ -1 \\ 7\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}-10 \\ 6 \\ -7\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}4 \\ -1 \\ 7\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}-10t \\ 6t \\ -7t\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}4-10t \\ -1+6t \\ 7-7t\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

where $t\in (-\infty ,\infty ).$ 

To get the equations for the line segment, we take only $t\in [0,1].$ Notice that substitution of $t=0$ in the above equation gives the coordinates of $P$ and substitution of $t=1$ gives the coordinates of $Q.$

Therefore, the parametric equations of the line segment $\overset{―}{PQ}$ are the following:

$$
{\begin{aligned}x=4-10t \\ y=-1+6t \\ z=7-7t\end{aligned}\,\,t\in [0,1]
$$
